title: Country Fried Chicken
subtitle: Buttermilk-soaked chicken in a crispy seasoned crust
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces soaked in buttermilk overnight, coated in heavily seasoned flour and fried until the crust shatters. A Southern diner staple served with mashed potato and gravy.
sourceNotes: Southern American deep-fried chicken tradition; the buttermilk soak is the defining step that separates country fried from plain fried chicken.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The buttermilk soak can go up to 24 hours in the fridge. Longer gives a more tender result.

content.text: Country fried chicken is bone-in chicken soaked in buttermilk and fried in a thick seasoned crust. The buttermilk makes the meat tender and the crust stays crisp. Fry at a steady medium heat so the chicken cooks through to the bone without the outside burning.

items.prepNote: for frying, enough to come 4cm up the pan

content.text: Place the chicken pieces in the large bowl. Pour over the buttermilk and hot sauce. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours.
Mix the flour, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, paprika, cayenne and onion powder in a separate large bowl.

Lift the chicken pieces from the buttermilk. Let the excess drip off. Dredge each piece in the seasoned flour. Press the flour onto the surface firmly, then dip back into the buttermilk and dredge in flour again for a thicker crust.
Heat the oil in the cast-iron skillet to a medium heat. A cube of bread should brown in 45 seconds.
Fry the chicken in batches of 3 or 4 pieces. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes per side. Do not crowd the pan or the temperature will drop.
The chicken is cooked when the juices run clear or an instant-read thermometer shows 75C at the thickest point.
Rest on a rack for 5 minutes before serving so the crust stays crisp.

items.symptom: The crust is dark but the chicken is raw inside.
items.fix: Lower the heat to medium. Fry low and slow so the heat reaches the bone before the crust burns.

items.symptom: The crust is pale and soft.
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough.
items.fix: Always check the oil temperature with a bread cube before adding chicken. Pale crust means the oil was cold.

items.symptom: The coating is thin and patchy.
items.fix: A second dip in buttermilk and flour gives the thick, shaggy crust that defines country fried chicken.
